edges.description: Estrogen restrains osteoclastogenesis largely by holding down RANKL relative to osteoprotegerin, so its withdrawal releases that brake directly. This is why bone loss accelerates sharply at menopause rather than gradually with age.
Tobacco shifts bone turnover toward loss on top of whatever else is driving remodelling, lowering attained bone mass. The responsible constituents and steps are not established in the cited source.
Therapeutic glucocorticoids suppress osteoblast function and lifespan while prolonging osteoclast survival, tipping remodelling toward resorption. It is the commonest secondary cause of the disease.
Unloading removes the mechanical signal that normally restrains resorption, and this entry carries a node specifically for it. Notably the loss is not fully reversible on return to gravity.

nodes.description: Increased osteoclast-mediated bone resorption relative to osteoblast- mediated bone formation leads to net bone loss. This imbalance accelerates with aging and estrogen deficiency.

evidence.snippet: aromatase activity and estrogen production are necessary for longitudinal bone growth, attainment of peak bone mass, the pubertal growth spurt, epiphyseal closure, and normal bone remodeling in young individuals.

evidence.reference_title: Aromatase deficiency, a rare syndrome: case report.
evidence.snippet: Estrogen deficiency can induce delayed epiphyseal closure, eunuchoid body habitus, osteopenia, and osteoporosis in both genders.

extraglandular aromatization of circulating androgen precursors is the major source of estrogen not only in men (since only 15% of circulating estradiol is released directly by the testis) but also in women after the menopause.

evidence.reference_title: Estrogen and bone: insights from estrogen-resistant, aromatase-deficient, and normal men.
evidence.snippet: studies in these unusual patients have stimulated research on defining the role of estrogen in regulating bone metabolism in normal adult and aging men, providing further insights into estrogen regulation of bone metabolism not only in men, but also in women.
Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis is the most common secondary cause of osteoporosis and the resulting fractures cause significant morbidity.

evidence.reference_title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of bone loss in space travelers.
evidence.snippet: Bone loss in space travelers is a major challenge for long-duration space exploration.

evidence.reference_title: Incomplete recovery of bone strength and trabecular microarchitecture at the distal tibia 1 year after return from long duration spaceflight.
evidence.snippet: nine of 17 astronauts did not fully recover tibia total BMD after 12-months

evidence.reference_title: Pre-flight exercise and bone metabolism predict unloading-induced bone loss due to spaceflight.
evidence.snippet: Increases in training volume predicted preservation of tibia bone strength and trabecular vBMD and thickness

evidence.reference_title: Targeting myostatin/activin A protects against skeletal muscle and bone loss during spaceflight.
evidence.snippet: Wild type mice lost significant muscle and bone mass during the 33 d spent in microgravity

nodes.description: Spaceflight induces a rapid and sustained increase in osteoclast-mediated bone resorption. Astronauts lose approximately 0.8% of bone mass per month in weight-bearing lower limb sites, with bone resorption markers plateauing at 113% above pre-flight levels within days of entering microgravity.

evidence.reference_title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of bone loss in space travelers.
evidence.snippet: Bone loss in space travelers is a major challenge for long-duration space exploration.

evidence.reference_title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of bone loss in space travelers.
evidence.snippet: microgravity-induced bone loss is a significant and unresolved health risk for space travelers

nodes.description: Increased RANKL and decreased osteoprotegerin (OPG) ratio promotes osteoclast differentiation and activation. Estrogen normally suppresses RANKL and increases OPG. Microgravity further exacerbates this imbalance by directly increasing the osteoblast RANKL/OPG ratio.

evidence.reference_title: Role of the IL-23/IL-17 Pathway in Rheumatic Diseases: An Overview.
evidence.snippet: The differentiation of osteoclasts is induced significantly in the presence of IL-17 either directly (207), or indirectly, through upregulation of RANKL.
with aging, individual differences in aromatase activity and thus in estrogen levels may significantly affect bone loss and fracture risk in both genders.

evidence.reference_title: Modeled microgravity stimulates osteoclastogenesis and bone resorption by increasing osteoblast RANKL/OPG ratio.
evidence.snippet: microgravity is capable to indirectly stimulate osteoclast formation and activity by regulating osteoblast secretion of crucial regulatory factors such as RANKL and OPG

evidence.reference_title: Osteoprotegerin is an effective countermeasure for spaceflight-induced bone loss in mice.
evidence.snippet: SF/VEH mice had lower BV/TV vs. GC/VEH mice, while SF/OPG-Fc mice had greater BV/TV than SF/VEH or GC/VEH

evidence.reference_title: The Effect of Tobacco Smoking on Bone Mass: An Overview of Pathophysiologic Mechanisms.
evidence.snippet: tobacco smoking causes an imbalance in bone turnover, leading to lower bone mass and making bone vulnerable to osteoporosis and fracture
